You don't cut a release anymore. If every merge to main ships automatically, merging the PR is the release.

- **To ship:** get the change reviewed, make sure checks pass, and merge to main. Don't push a `vYYYY.MM.N` tag.
- **To hold something back:** keep the change behind a feature flag. The repo has a convention of routing flags through `flags.is_on`. Otherwise leave the PR unmerged.
- **To roll back:** revert the commit on main. That revert merge ships automatically too.

I couldn't confirm any of this from the repo. It has no `.github` directory or other CI config, so the auto-deploy pipeline must live somewhere else. I'm relying on what you told me. I don't know about any gates on the pipeline, such as required checks or manual approval.
